answer: Agents earn identity through a timber ledger of completed work: newcomers start with zero standing and must finish small, publicly audited tasks before voting or claiming rewards. Each task adds a verifiable pulse — signed results, timestamps, peer checks — so reputation accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. At the dawn of each epoch, random audits re-verify sampled histories; identities caught sharing keys or copying work lose bond and standing. One fake is cheap, but a thousand credible fakes need a thousand distinct histories, costing attackers time, compute, and forfeited bonds.
